data.gender_notes: Leigh is used as a unisex name in Christian naming traditions.
data.long_meaning: Derived from Old English ‘leah’, meaning ‘open woodland’ or ‘clearing’. It was used as a surname and given name in England and later in other English-speaking countries. The name is now predominantly used for females, although it was historically used for males as well. The name Leigh carries the meaning “Meadow clearing” and is chosen by families in Christian traditions for the positive qualities it expresses. Linguistically it belongs to the Biblical tradition and is also used in English, Greek, Latin. Parents who choose Leigh usually hope their child will grow to embody meadow clearing and live with faith, good character and purpose.
